review_method: Direct inspection of selected source paragraphs and headings by the authoring agent. Not independent human annotation.
annotations: Links a reaction-discovery objective to representation design, automated experiments, and a tested screening outcome.
Explains why successive workflow components are needed and limits the discovery output to initial reactivity hits.
Defines the related modeling task, selected reaction population, and atom-level prediction target before evaluation.
Summarizes workflow contributions and makes the proposed change in the development bottleneck conditional on maintained accuracy.
Frames an unfavorable machine-learning result through comparison with a simple frequency-based explanation.
Connects a limitation in available reaction records to a proposal for systematic data generation.
States data exclusions and successive population definitions while narrowing the prediction task.
Relates disappointing model performance to data-generation practices and derives a concrete comparison requirement.
Names electronic-structure calculations and trajectory simulations separately when presenting pathway and product-distribution findings.
Explains molecular design choices through the intended reaction possibilities and control of conformational freedom.
Opens the result sequence with a figure-linked candidate geometry and possible outcomes rather than a performance statistic.
Distinguishes located structures, trajectory outcomes, and an observed geometric correlation in the summary.
Connects scaffold choice with complementary experimental and computational tests of reactivity explanations.
Defines a scaffold-specific comparison between measured kinetics and calculated predictions.
Uses competing electronic and steric expectations to motivate the selected substitution series.
Keeps the mostly modest effects visible while identifying an exception for further interpretation.
Presents tunable scaffold design through the linked objectives of reactivity, stability, and selectivity.
Motivates heteroatom combinations with a stability–reactivity tradeoff before announcing the synthetic and computational study.
Explains a synthetic obstacle before describing the route and the observed product outcome.
Connects synthetic access and reactivity observations to a design interpretation while leaving wider application under investigation.
Connects tunable reaction behavior with orthogonal ligation design and biological tests.
Assigns different roles to computational analyses, predicted reaction pairs, and subsequent demonstrations.
Reports an initial calculation–experiment mismatch and uses comparative agreement to motivate the computational choice.
Links computational design to experimentally assessed systems and distinguishes demonstrated uses from further development.
Pairs experimental rate comparisons with calculations intended to explain their origin.
Moves from established chemistry and a computational expectation to an explicit set of comparative substrates.
Defines measurement conditions and the kinetic observable before reporting the individual reaction comparisons.
Summarizes the tested substrate scope while explicitly leaving a decomposition mechanism under investigation.
Positions improved synthetic accessibility alongside retained useful reactivity and a biological application.
Connects a specific scaffold modification with synthetic practicality and the intended chemical function.
Integrates synthetic steps with observed outcomes and marks a proposed selectivity explanation as tentative.
Combines preparation, functional performance, and biological testing in the closing account.
An experimental section occurs before Results and Discussion in this article.
A substantive results section uses a scaffold-and-reactivity topic heading rather than a declarative finding.
A numbered part heading names the chemical prediction task within the larger workflow.
